claims.object_text: severe epilepsy and global developmental delay
claims.quote: a de novo pathogenic missense variant in GRIA3 (c.1979G>C; p. R660T) identified in a 1-year-old female patient with severe epilepsy and global developmental delay.
a de novo pathogenic missense variant in GRIA3 (c.1979G>C; p. R660T)
a gain of function (GoF) variant in GRIA3 may cause epileptic encephalopathy and global developmental delay in a female subject by enhancing synaptic transmission.
GLUA3_R660T showed slower desensitization and deactivation kinetics compared to wildtype (wt) GLUA3 receptors.
Substantial non-desensitized currents were observed with the mutant but not for wt GLUA3 with prolonged exposure to glutamate.

claims.object_text: slowed decay kinetics with non-desensitized steady state currents when co-expressed with GLUA2
claims.quote: When co-expressed with GLUA2, the decay kinetics were similarly slowed in GLUA2/A3_R660T with non-desensitized steady state currents.

claims.object_text: slower miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents (mEPSCs) in transfected neurons
claims.quote: In cultured cerebellar granule neurons, miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents (mEPSCs) were significantly slower in R660T transfected cells than those expressing wt GLUA3.

claims.object_text: overexpressed in hippocampal CA1 neurons by in utero electroporation
claims.quote: When overexpressed in hippocampal CA1 neurons by in utero electroporation, the evoked EPSCs and mEPSCs were slower in neurons expressing R660T mutant compared to those expressing wt GLUA3.

claims.object_text: slower evoked EPSCs and mEPSCs in CA1 neurons expressing R660T
claims.quote: the evoked EPSCs and mEPSCs were slower in neurons expressing R660T mutant compared to those expressing wt GLUA3.
